name: Threat Hunting - Methodology & Process
description: Structured threat hunting methodology used in SOC environments. Threat hunting is a proactive, human-led practice that searches for advanced threats evading automated detection. Covers the full hunting cycle, team roles, and integration with incident response.
source: CDSA Module 04: Introduction to Threat Hunting & Hunting With Elastic
notes:
=== Threat Hunting Definition ===
Proactive, human-led practice that systematically searches for stealthy advanced threats
evading existing security solutions. Goal: reduce dwell time by detecting threats
early in the kill chain.

=== 5-Phase Hunting Process ===
1. Setting the Stage (Planning)
   → Identify high-value assets (crown jewels)
   → Research attacker TTPs from threat intel
   → Enable logging (Sysmon, PowerShell, Zeek, Windows Events)
   → Configure SIEM, EDR, IDS tools

2. Formulating Hypotheses
   → Based on: threat intel, industry alerts, tool alerts, intuition
   → Must be testable and specific
   → Example: 'Stuxbot delivers invoice.one phishing files via Gmail'

3. Designing the Hunt
   → Identify data sources: Windows logs, Sysmon, Zeek, PS logs
   → Define KQL queries, correlation rules, IOC lists
   → Select tools: SIEM (Kibana/Splunk), EDR, packet analyzers

4. Data Gathering & Examination (active hunt)
   → Execute queries against data sources
   → Analyze results: confirm or refute hypothesis
   → Pivot on new findings — iterative process
   → Document evidence at each step

5. After the Hunt
   → Update threat intelligence platforms with new IOCs
   → Improve SIEM detection rules based on findings
   → Refine IR playbooks
   → Communicate findings to SOC/CISO

=== When to Hunt ===
• New adversary or vulnerability intelligence disclosed
• New IOCs linked to a known threat actor targeting your sector
• Multiple simultaneous network anomalies detected
• During active IR — hunt for lateral spread in parallel
• Periodic proactive hunts (scheduled, ongoing)

=== Team Roles ===
• Threat Hunter — TTP expertise, executes hypotheses
• Threat Intel Analyst — collects/analyzes feeds, OSINT
• Incident Responder — containment/eradication once threat confirmed
• Data Analyst/Scientist — statistical and ML-based analysis
• Security Engineer — tunes tools, implements detections
• SOC Manager — coordinates team, communicates upward

=== Threat Intel Types ===
Strategic   → high-level, for executives. Nation-state actors, industry risk.
Operational → campaign details, attacker infrastructure, TTPs per attack.
Tactical    → IOCs: IPs, hashes, domains, registry keys, mutexes.

=== Pyramid of Pain (IOC Prioritization) ===
[Top]    TTPs             → hardest for attacker to change; best for detection
         Tools            → specific binaries/RATs
         Network Artefacts → C2 domains, JA3, User-Agents
         Domain Names
         IP Addresses
[Base]   Hash Values      → trivial recompile defeats; least useful alone

→ Push detections UP the pyramid. Hash-only = easily evaded.
   TTP-based Sigma/YARA rules survive tool updates.
